increments.title: A shared-only entry is no candidate for the mandatory auto-add
increments.goal: A fresh roster over a catalogue whose mandatory-looking entry lives only in `sharedSelectionEntries` gets no selection of it at force level, while mandatory rules declared at the catalogue root keep being set automatically and the entry stays choosable where the catalogue offers it.
criteria: An entry that a catalogue holds only in `sharedSelectionEntries` is no candidate for the mandatory auto-add, however its constraints read: a fresh roster over such a catalogue gets no selection of that entry at force level. Pin it on an inline fixture that mirrors the real shape — the entry in `sharedSelectionEntries` with `type="upgrade"`, no own sub-options, `min=1 scope="roster" includeChildSelections="true"`, offered through a shared group a character links — and name `Pure of Heart` / `Honours` in a comment. verify: `npx vitest run src/roster/listRules src/hooks/useRoster`

A mandatory list rule declared at the catalogue root is still set automatically, in both root forms: as a root `selectionEntry`, and as a root `entryLink` whose target is a shared entry carrying the `min`. verify: `npx vitest run src/hooks/useRoster.mandatoryAutoAdd src/hooks/useRoster.costedMandatoryAutoAdd` stay green, plus a new case for the root-`entryLink`-onto-shared-target form.
The entry stays choosable where the catalogue does offer it: on a character that links the group holding it, the option is offered and can be taken. verify: `npx vitest run src/roster`
The JSDoc of `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections` states the rule and names ADR 0032, so the write model and the engine read the same on this point.
increments.note: The load-bearing slice: it changes what the auto-add may reach, and both guard criteria (root forms still auto-added, the entry still choosable on a character) exist only to bound that one change, so they are judged with it.

increments.title: A wrongly added selection can be removed by hand, and the fix ships
increments.goal: A roster saved before the fix can be freed of the wrongly added selection — or the run records that today's lock never held it — and the repository is green and versioned for release.
criteria: A roster that already carries the wrongly added selection can be freed of it by hand — the mandatory lock must not hold a selection at a place the catalogue never offered. Establish first whether the lock does that today; if it does not, record that in `docs/issues/0153-honour-only-reachable-from-a-hero-is-auto-added-to-the-army/issue.md` and leave the code alone.
`npx vitest run`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` are green. verify: `npx vitest run && npm run lint && npm run typecheck`
`package.json` carries version `2.0.4` — a user-visible fix — set with `node scripts/release.js patch` and committed on the issue branch.
increments.note: Its first criterion is an open question about existing behaviour whose answer decides whether any code moves, so it cannot be a direct increment; the release gate rides with it because it is the last slice.

steps.label: decompose

rulings: Cut the issue into two increments rather than one per criterion, because criteria 1-3 and 5 all bound the single change to the auto-add candidate set and only criterion 4 opens a separate behaviour question; wrong costs one extra research-build-review chain that a re-cut can add after inc-1 lands.

Put the green-suite gate and the version bump in the last increment instead of an increment of their own, because a release step is not a change a reader judges on its own; wrong costs a version bump that lands late, which is a one-command correction.

Left the criterion-4 lock question inside its increment rather than raising it as a question, because the issue itself asks the run to establish the current behaviour first and the answer is readable from the code; wrong costs that increment reporting a finding instead of a fix, which the issue already allows for.
return.summary: Cut issue 0153 into two increments over the codemap of ten files. Criterion 1 -> inc-1; criterion 2 -> inc-1; criterion 3 -> inc-1; criterion 4 -> inc-2; criterion 5 -> inc-1; criterion 6 -> inc-2; criterion 7 -> inc-2. inc-1 is the load-bearing slice: it narrows what the mandatory auto-add may reach, and criteria 2, 3 and 5 exist only to bound that one change, so splitting them off would build and review the same edit three times. inc-2 carries the open question about the mandatory lock on already-saved rosters, whose answer may be a code change or a recorded finding, plus the repository-wide green gate and the 2.0.4 bump. Both are `full`: inc-1 needs new tests over an inline fixture, and inc-2 turns on a behaviour nobody has established yet. Rejected a per-criterion cut (seven chains for one edit) and rejected a single increment (criterion 4 can be blocked or answered without touching code, independently of the auto-add fix).
